title: Bentlage Monastery in Rheine with the Westphalian Gallery of the LWL
content: Tourismus NRW e.V., The monastery complex in Rheine in Münsterland directly on the banks of the Ems. # Bentlage Monastery. In addition to the important collection on the history of the monastery, it houses the Westphalian Gallery and is a meeting place for renowned contemporary artists - and cyclists. The listed complex, which has been largely preserved in its original state, also offers space for modernity and presents works by important artists in the "Westphalian Gallery" of the LWL Museum of Art and Culture.r Kunst und Kultur presents works by important artists such as August Macke, Josef Albers, Wilhelm Morgner, Emil Schumacher and Otto Modersohn, who was one of the founders of the Worpswede artists' colony. In addition, workshops and symposia as well as a printing workshop and studio apartment attract artists of international standing to the recreational area on the banks of the River Ems, which is also a hub for several cycle routes in the Münsterland region.

title: St. Lucia (Harsewinkel) - myCityHunt.com
content: # St. Lucia Harsewinkel. ## St. Lucia. St. Lucia in Harsewinkel, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, is an architectural gem and a symbol of the town's rich historical tapestry. This Catholic parish church, with its towering spire and intricate neo-Gothic design, stands as a testament to centuries of faith, craftsmanship, and community spirit. ### The History of St. Lucia. The first documented mention of Harsewinkel's church dates back to approximately 1050 in a record from the Freckenhorst Monastery, referring to it as Haswinklia. The church's dedication to St. Lucia suggests a historical link to the church in Warendorf. In the early 12th century, the Wadenhart Chapel was established in the nearby community of Hundingen, now Marienfeld, as an extension of St. Lucia. The architectural history of St. Lucia is as rich and varied as its spiritual heritage. ### The Community and St. Lucia. In conclusion, St. Lucia in Harsewinkel is more than just a church; it is a symbol of the town's rich heritage and a beacon of faith and community spirit.

title: Willkommen in der Hotel-Residence Klosterpforte – History
content: # History of the Klosterpforte. The Hotel-Residence Klosterpforte is situated in a romantic spot directly in front of the gates of an 800-year-old monastery. Already in 1412 one of the monks made a drawing of the grounds of the monastery in Marienfeld. The monastery church was built in the time from 1185 to 1222 and is now used as a parish church. On the one-kilometre-long tour of the premises a total of 12 steles along the path inform visitors about the history of the monastery and the grounds as well as the foundation of the monastery and the individual buildings on the premises. In our chronicle you can see historic pictures of the Klosterpforte (monastery gate) and the development of the area up to the present day. It its place a new building complex is built including a large wellness area with a sauna, swimming pool, hotel rooms as well as business and conference rooms.
